clue.text: Activists making gain excitedly embraced by people in tents

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside the arms of the other piece, so it sits within

parts.note: people sleeping in tents are campers

indicators.note: done excitedly, the letters of gain are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A rally of protesters gets worked up about some gain they have made while living in a tent camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' jumbles the clue's own word gain, and 'embraced by' sets that inside the tent-dwellers; 'making' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Activists who push for a cause are those running a campaign, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Copper not entirely cross with you and me — a fluffy wet type?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A puzzled description of something soft and damp, tacked on to a chemistry and grammar puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims MULE to MUL. The question mark flags that the definition describes rather than defines: a cloud of this type is fluffy and holds water.
explanation.definitionFit: This puffy, heaped cloud type looks fluffy and carries moisture, so it is a fluffy wet sort of cloud.

clue.text: Characters inside home agreed to be miserly

indicators.note: characters inside points to a run of letters sitting within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone agreed at home to tighten the purse strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserly and scanty both describe a mean, insufficient amount, as with a scant portion.

clue.text: Like some lorries lacking rear piece, say

indicators.note: lacking its rear piece means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: articulated lorries have a cab and trailer joined at a pivot

explanation.surface: A description of lorries missing the trailer at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: An articulated lorry (US: semi-trailer truck) has a separate trailer, so a lorry 'lacking rear piece' sounds literal. Dropping the last letter instead gives the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate a thought is to put it into words, to express or utter it.

clue.text: Lark, partridge, pheasant …?

definitions.meaning: a lark is a bit of fun or a jape, as in playing a silly trick
partridge and pheasant are birds shot for sport and food, examples of the class

explanation.surface: A list of birds, with the songbird lark the odd one out among shooting birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The lark looks like the first bird of the list, but it means a jape.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is fun or sport; partridge and pheasant are wild birds hunted, both senses of the same word.

clue.text: Needed hospital facility, wasn't well

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
someone who was not well ailed

explanation.surface: A patient needed the hospital because they were not well.
explanation.definitionFit: If a plan entails something, that thing is required or involved by it, so entailed means necessitated.

clue.text: End of week with tot being given a fruit

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, the last day of the week
to tot up is to add, giving a sum

explanation.surface: At the weekend a small child is handed a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child but means an addition.
explanation.definitionFit: This small loose-skinned citrus, much like a mandarin, is a fruit.

clue.text: Concise treaty

definitions.meaning: concise means brief, packed into little space
a treaty is a formal agreement between parties, a pact

explanation.surface: A short, crisp description of a treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: Concise matches the adjective sense of tightly packed; a treaty is a formal agreement or pact.

clue.text: A politician in church preached, becoming oily

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
to orate is to speak like a preacher, so preached is orated

explanation.surface: A politician gives a sermon in church and grows unctuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' is a link word. Camphorated oil is an old liniment, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated with camphor, as in the rubbing oil sold in chemists, describes something oily.

clue.text: Changed, being dull, given a time inside

indicators.note: inside means these letters go within the word for dull

parts.note: a dull colour or sound is muted

explanation.surface: Something altered, becoming dull after being left for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has mutated has undergone change, especially genetic alteration.

clue.text: Leader's type to writhe in anguish

indicators.note: letters made to writhe twist about into a new order

explanation.surface: A ruler's sort of person squirms in torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in anguish is acting in despair, frantically or hopelessly, which this adverb describes.

clue.text: Flow of water unfortunate, river infiltrating club

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside the next word

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club
ill luck is unfortunate, so ill can mean unfortunate

explanation.surface: An unlucky river breaks into a club, as a flood might.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the channel of water that drives a mill wheel, a current or stream of water.

clue.text: Little dogs outside home? They may be very pretty

indicators.note: outside means the young dogs surround the next piece

parts.note: little dogs are pups
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Puppies kept outdoors are, it seems, very pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole closing sentence: these are attractive people pictured on posters.
explanation.definitionFit: These posters show glamorous people, so the subjects are usually very pretty.

clue.text: Very good having miss to entertain you in ship's compartment

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

indicators.note: to entertain means to take in another piece as a guest

parts.note: to miss a chance is to lose it
thou is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A virtuous young woman hosts a guest aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a young woman but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the enclosed deckhouse from which a vessel is steered, a compartment on a ship.

clue.text: One who entertains a lot of people

definitions.meaning: someone who entertains guests at home
a multitude or great crowd, as in a heavenly throng

explanation.surface: An entertainer with a big crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The person receiving guests is one sense; a multitude or throng is the other.

clue.text: I half-read a little, sadly lacking education?

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are in a sorry, disordered state
half of the word read means its first two letters only

explanation.surface: A confession of having only half-read a little, sadly lacking schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-' takes RE from 'read'; 'sadly' shuffles I, RE and ALITTLE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to read or write lacks basic schooling; the question mark hints the person is unlettered.

clue.text: Eastern relation going potty

indicators.note: going potty, or mad, means the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A relative from the East is losing their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: This word describes things from Asia or the Orient, the East.

clue.text: Agent has a share in process of putting things right again

definitions.text: process of putting things right again

parts.note: a rep, or representative, acts as an agent
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A sales agent takes his portion during the fix-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Making amends for a wrong, as with war damages paid, puts things right again.

clue.text: Out of breath decorating? Not I!

indicators.note: not I means the letter I is left out

parts.note: decorating a room is painting it

explanation.surface: A decorator, puffed out, protests that someone else is doing the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not I!' reads as a refusal but drops I from PAINTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasping for air after effort is being out of breath.

clue.text: Second letter to the Corinthians

parts.note: the second epistle of Paul suggests the Bible, but the ancient Corinthians spoke Greek, whose alphabet's second letter is meant

explanation.walkthrough: The clue wants you to think of Paul's Second Epistle to the Corinthians; instead it is the second letter of the alphabet the Corinthians used.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth was a Greek city, and this is the second character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Look at dictator submerged in river

indicators.note: submerged in means placed inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: Peering at a tyrant drowned in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect or scrutinise something is to look at it closely.

clue.text: Greeting given to ruler on a walk

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Someone says hello to the monarch out on a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tramping across country is out on a long walk.

clue.text: Offer to look after Her Majesty

parts.note: to tend is to look after
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A proposal to take care of the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a formal bid or proposal, as in offering to supply goods.

clue.text: Mushroom — I will have it dunked in milky drink!

indicators.note: dunked in means put inside the drink

parts.note: a shake, short for milkshake, is a milky drink

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly dips a mushroom in their milkshake.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese fungus, sold widely in shops, is an edible mushroom.

clue.text: What's served up in their breakfast? Cheese

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means read from bottom to top
in signals the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question about what a family is given at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds EIRB within 'their breakfast'; 'served up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft French variety from the Île-de-France region is a cheese.

clue.text: Fault admitted by the German fellow lacking direction

indicators.note: admitted by means let inside the other word

parts.note: der is German for the
a geological fault is a rift

explanation.surface: A German man without purpose owns up to a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wandering aimlessly through life, without purpose, is a drifting sort of person.

clue.text: Usefulness or uselessness with leader absent?

indicators.note: with leader absent means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: futility is uselessness

explanation.surface: A riddle: is something useful or useless when the boss is away?
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that removing one letter turns uselessness into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Utility is the quality of being serviceable, so it means practical value.

clue.text: Big bird in Donegal flying with glee

indicators.note: letters flying about land in a new order

explanation.surface: A large bird soars happily over Donegal, a county in the north-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This raptor is one of the largest birds of prey in Europe.
